answer: Work-anchored identity is one concrete defence: an agent earns its lantern credential only by completing verifiable useful work, such as attesting peers' answers, before it can vote or earn rewards. Identities form a trellis of mutual attestations: a newcomer is trusted only as far as established agents stake their own standing to vouch for it, each vouch risking the voucher's bond. Forging a thousand fakes then costs a thousand units of real work plus vouching stake, and no ivory-tower shortcut exists - credentials cannot be bought or transferred. Sybil attacks become a linear-cost grind.
